newsitem.title: SPAIN: US agrees to help Spain on Chile killings probe.
newsitem.headline: US agrees to help Spain on Chile killings probe.

text.p: The United States has agreed to cooperate with Spain's High Court investigating killings of Spanish citizens during the former Chilean military regime of General Augusto Pinochet, judicial sources said on Wednesday.

"In light of such an important issue, the fact that the United States has decided to respect international treaties and Spanish jurisdiction will be an important precedent for the future," a lawyer for the prosecution told Reuters.

U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno has instructed her department to assist in investigations led by Spanish judge Manuel Garcia Castellon into the death of Spaniards during Pinochet's rule from 1973 to 1990, the Spanish newspaper El Pais reported Wednesday.

Reno has also ordered that Castellon be given access to files on the dictatorship held in the archives of the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), El Pais said.
Castellon is investigating the disappearance of about 10 Spaniards including an official from the United Nations' Latin American Economic Commission, Carmelo Soria.

The Spaniards were among some 3,000 people killed after being detained by security forces during the rightist dictatorship of Pinochet, who took power in a coup favoured by the then-U.S. government because it toppled Marxist president Salvador Allende.
Pinochet, 81, remains commander-in-chief of the Chilean army until next March.
Castellon's request to the United States to help investigations was supported by a number of Democratic members of Congress including Massachusetts Senator Edward Kennedy, according to El Pais.
In addition to being given access to secret files, Castellon will be able to interview FBI officers on the killings, the prosecuting attorney said.
"The magistrate will come to the United States and it seems that the testimonies will be taken in Washington."
Chile's current democratic government has said it will not recognise the authority of Castellon's court to try Pinochet for the Spanish killings.

Chilean Justice Minister Soledad Alvear told officials in Madrid at the end of May that her government would not accept the jurisdiction of courts in other countries over crimes committed on Chilean soil, even if they involved foreign citizens.
Castellon has not yet asked Chile to help in his investigations.
